question: Which among the following is a part of URL (Uniform Resource Locator)?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Port number**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Port number** is a component of a URL (Uniform Resource Locator).
 
• A URL is used to specify addresses on the World Wide Web.
 
• It typically consists of the protocol (such as HTTP or HTTPS), the domain name, and may include a port number, path, query string, and fragment identifier.
 
• The port number is used to identify a specific process or service on the server. For example, HTTP typically uses port 80, while HTTPS uses port 443.
 
• Including the port number in the URL allows communication with the correct service or application on the server.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A URL can also include a **username and password** for authentication, although this is less common.
 
• The **domain name** part of the URL can be either an IP address or a human-readable name that is resolved to an IP address via DNS (Domain Name System).
 
• The **path** specifies the exact resource within the domain that the client wants to access.
 
• **Query strings** are used to pass additional parameters to the server, typically in the format of key-value pairs.
 
• The **fragment identifier** is used to point to a specific section within a resource, usually within an HTML document.
